::: {#def-population-distribution}
#### Population distribution

The **population distribution** of a variable $X$ is the distribution of $X$
for a unit [chosen at random](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-random-choice)
from a population (@def-population):
the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) that $X$ falls in a set $A$ is

$$\Pf{A} \eqdef \Pr(X \in A),$$

where the probability refers to the random choice of the unit.
:::

::: {.remark .notes}
A population may be finite or infinite.
For a finite population $U$ of $N$ units, with $X(u)$ the value of $X$ for unit $u$,
the random choice gives each unit probability $1/N$, so

$$\Pf{A} = \frac{\abs{\set{u \in U : X(u) \in A}}}{N}.$$

An infinite population, such as all the coin flips a coin could ever produce,
is described directly by a distribution.
The population distribution can equally be described by its
cumulative distribution function $F(t) = \Pf{(-\infty, t]}$
or, when it has one, by its probability mass or density function.
:::
